content.text:
What kind of fairy tale is Sleeping Beauty?

Sleeping Beauty is a classic fairy tale about a princess who falls into a deep sleep because of a curse and, after a long time, is awakened by love. It carries the warm message that even in the midst of hardship, hope never disappears.

content.alt: Sleeping Beauty - The original Sleeping Beauty story
content.text:
The original Sleeping Beauty story

The versions by Charles Perrault (1697) and the Brothers Grimm (1812, "Little Briar Rose") are the most famous. The heart of the tale is the curse from a fairy who was not invited, the princess falling asleep after pricking her finger on a spindle, and her awakening a hundred years later. A kind fairy softens the curse of death into a deep sleep instead.

content.alt: Sleeping Beauty - A summary of the Sleeping Beauty story
content.text:
A summary of the Sleeping Beauty story

Because of the fairy's curse, the princess pricks her finger on a spindle and falls into a deep sleep, and the whole castle falls asleep with her. After many long years, someone who finds the castle awakens the princess with a heartfelt, sincere love, and the sleeping castle and all its people wake up too, returning to their happy everyday life once more.

content.alt: Sleeping Beauty - The moral of Sleeping Beauty
content.text:
The moral of Sleeping Beauty

The heart of it is that if you never lose hope even in the midst of hardship, good days will come in the end. You can also talk with your child about the power of sincerity and love.

content.alt: Sleeping Beauty - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Read the falling-asleep scene in a soft, slow voice, then brighten your tone for the awakening scene. Ask, "How would it feel to wait for such a long time?" to talk about patience and hope, and you can even sing a lullaby together. Best suited for ages 4–7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is Sleeping Beauty good for?
A. It's best suited for ages 4–7. With its calm, gentle flow, it also makes a lovely bedtime story.

Q. Is it the same as "The Sleeping Beauty in the Wood"?
A. Yes, it's the same story. Depending on the version, the title and some details differ slightly.

Q. What kinds of conversations are good to have?
A. Talk together about "waiting and hope" and "the power of a sincere heart."
